correctness.rationale: The code/normalization bijection is proved by equality of generator-row spans; the pairwise edit-distance/LCS reduction includes constant/nonconstant pairs and every nonidentity affine symbol transform. LCS for two permutations equals strict LIS of the induced positional permutation. Exhausting all (q-2)! suffix permutations and all q(q-1)-1 nonidentity affine transforms therefore exhausts the exact claim. Two separately implemented C++17 verifiers, bit-parallel LCS and strict-LIS, agree on all eight field sizes, with ordinary O(q^2) LCS cross-check for every transformation at q<=7. For q=11 they independently give (L6,L7,L8,L9,L10)=(128045,213170,20942,714,9), totaling 362880 orders; all rows sum to (q-2)! and verify nonzero multipliers bijective. At q=13 a separate ordinary-LCS check agrees with LIS for all 155 transforms of the stated vector; their length histogram (3:6,4:37,5:73,6:39) proves exact radius six. The result is finite and does not infer infinite behavior from samples.

value.rationale: A recent, explicitly stated research question asks which full-length Reed–Solomon evaluation orders achieve strong synchronization-error correction. The full finite distributions answer this natural structural question for every prime-power field size through eleven, not just an arbitrary unmotivated statistic. In particular field eleven divides all 362880 distinct codes into five exact robustness classes, including 128045 achieving its Hamming correction radius; field eight has a strict performance deficit. The verified field-thirteen witness and exhaustive exclusion of smaller field sizes establish the first transition to better-than-Hamming synchronization correction. These facts are not mere restatements of the already-known zero-radius characterization or a tiny bound improvement; the finite classification and sharp field threshold have a concrete code-design interpretation.
